q: What is Azure Container Registry used for?
opts: Storing and managing private container images and artifacts
exp: ACR is a managed private registry for OCI images and artifacts.

q: Which CLI command creates a Standard container registry?
opts: az acr create -g RG1 -n myacr --sku Standard
exp: az acr create with --sku Basic, Standard, or Premium.

q: Before pushing with docker, how do you authenticate to ACR using your Entra identity?
opts: docker login with your Entra password
exp: az acr login gets a token and configures Docker.

q: What is the full image name format for pushing to registry myacr?
exp: Images are tagged with the registry login server, <name>.azurecr.io.

q: Which ACR SKU is required for private endpoints (Private Link)?
exp: Private Link, geo-replication, and content trust require Premium.

q: A CI pipeline needs to push images to ACR. Least-privilege role?
exp: AcrPush allows push and pull; AcrPull is pull-only.

q: Images must rebuild automatically when their base image is updated. Which feature?
opts: ACR Tasks with base image update triggers
exp: ACR Tasks can trigger on source commits and base image updates.

q: How do you copy an image from Docker Hub into ACR without pulling it locally?
exp: az acr import copies images server-side.

q: Why is the ACR admin account discouraged for production?
opts: It's a single shared username and password with full push/pull rights and no per-user auditing
exp: Use Entra identities or tokens with scoped permissions instead.

q: Which CLI command creates a container instance with a public DNS label?
opts: az container create -g RG1 -n web --image mcr.microsoft.com/azuredocs/aci-helloworld --dns-name-label myweb --ports 80
exp: az container create with --dns-name-label and --ports exposes the container.

q: Which CLI command shows a running container instance's logs?
exp: az container logs retrieves stdout and stderr.

q: You need an interactive shell inside a running container in ACI. Use:
exp: az container exec runs a command inside the container.

q: Container data must persist after the container stops. What do you do?
opts: Mount an Azure Files share as a volume
exp: ACI storage is ephemeral; Azure Files provides persistence.

q: How are CPU and memory assigned in ACI?
opts: You request vCPU and memory per container (for example, --cpu 1 --memory 1.5) and are billed per second
exp: ACI resources are requested per container.

q: A container instance must reach a database on a private IP in VNet1 without a public IP. What do you do?
opts: Deploy the container group into a delegated subnet in VNet1
exp: ACI can be deployed into a VNet subnet delegated to Microsoft.ContainerInstance/containerGroups.

q: How do you pass a database password to an ACI container so it isn't shown in the portal?
exp: Secure environment variables aren't exposed in container properties.

q: How do you deploy a multi-container group (app plus sidecar) to ACI?
opts: With a YAML file or ARM template defining the container group
With one az container create per container in the same group
exp: Multi-container groups are defined with YAML or ARM/Bicep.

q: How do you scale an ACI deployment?
opts: ACI has no built-in autoscale; deploy more container groups or change resource requests (redeploy)
exp: For autoscale, use Container Apps or AKS.

q: In Azure Container Apps, what's the boundary that groups apps sharing a VNet and Log Analytics workspace?
exp: Apps in the same environment share networking and logging.

q: In Container Apps, what is a revision?
opts: An immutable snapshot of a container app version
exp: Changes to revision-scoped settings create new revisions.

q: Send 20% of traffic to a new version of a container app and 80% to the old one. What do you configure?
opts: Multiple revision mode with traffic splitting (weights)
exp: Multiple revision mode allows weighted traffic splits for canary releases.

q: Which Container Apps scale rule type scales on concurrent HTTP requests?
exp: HTTP rules scale on concurrent requests; KEDA scalers handle events; CPU and memory rules are also available.

q: A container app should be reachable only from other apps in the same environment. Which ingress setting?
exp: Internal ingress restricts access to the environment or VNet.

q: A scheduled nightly batch task should run in Container Apps and then exit. Which resource?
exp: Jobs run to completion with manual, schedule, or event triggers.

q: Which TWO services can scale containers automatically based on load without you managing Kubernetes?
opts: Azure App Service (Web App for Containers) with autoscale
exp: Container Apps and App Service support autoscaling. ACI doesn't autoscale; ACR stores images.

q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: Container Apps can scale to zero replicas
exp: Container Apps scales to zero and supports Dapr; ACI runs Windows containers; geo-replication is Premium only.

q: Which App Service tier is intended for free development and testing, with shared infrastructure and no custom domains?
exp: Free and Shared are for dev/test with limitations.

q: Which tier is the lowest that supports custom domains with SSL bindings and dedicated compute?
exp: Basic adds dedicated VMs, custom domains, and TLS, with manual scaling.

q: An app needs full network isolation in a single-tenant environment inside your VNet with very high scale. Which tier?
exp: Isolated tiers run in an App Service Environment.

q: Three web apps run in one App Service plan with 2 instances. How many instances does each app run on?
opts: 2 — every app runs on all instances of the plan
exp: Apps share the plan's instances; scaling the plan scales every app in it.

q: Can you move a web app to an App Service plan in a different region?
opts: No — the plan must be in the same resource group and region (webspace); create the app in the new region instead
exp: Apps can move between plans only within the same region and resource group combination.

q: What's the maximum instance count of a Standard App Service plan?
exp: Basic up to 3, Standard up to 10, Premium v3 up to 30, Isolated up to 100.

q: An app should scale out instantly based on HTTP traffic, without writing autoscale rules (Premium v2/v3). Which feature?
exp: Automatic scaling lets the platform scale based on HTTP traffic for Premium v2/v3.

q: Which CLI command creates a web app in an existing plan?
opts: az webapp create -g RG1 -p plan1 -n myapp123 --runtime "DOTNETCORE:8.0"
exp: az webapp create needs a resource group, plan, globally unique name, and runtime.

q: Which CLI command creates a Linux App Service plan at the S1 tier?
opts: az appservice plan create -g RG1 -n plan1 --sku S1 --is-linux
exp: az appservice plan create with --sku and --is-linux.

q: An app stores its database connection string. Where should non-secret settings and secret references go?
opts: App settings / connection strings (with Key Vault references for secrets)
exp: App settings are environment variables; Key Vault references keep secrets out of config.

q: A Key Vault reference in App Service settings fails to resolve. What's the most common missing piece?
opts: The app's managed identity lacks permission (for example, Key Vault Secrets User) on the vault
The vault must be in another region
exp: The app needs an identity with secret get permission on the vault.

q: Continuous WebJobs stop running when there's no traffic. Which setting fixes this?
exp: Always On keeps the app loaded (Basic tier and above).

q: A stateless app behind multiple instances has unbalanced load because users stick to one instance. What do you disable?
exp: ARR affinity pins clients to instances; disable it for stateless apps.

q: App Service should stop routing traffic to an instance that fails a /health endpoint check. Which feature?
exp: Health check removes unhealthy instances from the load balancer rotation.

q: How many deployment slots (including production) does the Standard tier allow?
exp: Standard allows 5 slots; Premium allows 20.

q: Which CLI command swaps the staging slot with production?
opts: az webapp deployment slot swap -g RG1 -n myapp --slot staging --target-slot production
exp: az webapp deployment slot swap performs the swap.

q: You want 10% of production users to hit the staging slot for testing. Which feature?
exp: Testing in production routes a percentage of traffic to a slot.

q: Every time code is pushed to staging, it must automatically swap to production after warm-up. Which feature?
exp: Auto swap swaps a slot into production after deployment and warm-up.

q: To map the apex domain contoso.com (no www) to an App Service app, which DNS records are used?
opts: An A record with the app's IP, plus a TXT record asuid for verification
exp: CNAMEs aren't allowed at the apex, so use an A record plus TXT verification.

q: All HTTP requests to an app must be redirected to HTTPS. Which setting?
exp: HTTPS Only redirects HTTP to HTTPS.

q: A wildcard certificate (*.contoso.com) must secure several App Service apps. What should you use?
opts: Import the certificate (from Key Vault or a PFX upload) — managed certificates don't support wildcards
A Let's Encrypt cert via the portal
exp: Wildcards require an imported or App Service certificate.

q: An internal web app must be reachable ONLY from your VNet and on-premises (over VPN), with no public exposure. Which feature?
opts: A private endpoint for the app (and disabling public access)
exp: Private endpoints provide private inbound access; VNet integration is for outbound traffic.

q: Where are custom (scheduled) App Service backups stored?
opts: In a storage account container you choose
exp: Custom backups write to a configured storage account. Automatic backups are platform-managed.

ctx: App1 runs on a Basic B1 Linux plan. Requirements: staging slot, CPU-based autoscale, a free TLS certificate for www.contoso.com, and outbound access to a VM's private IP.
q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: B1 supports a staging deployment slot
A free managed certificate can be used for www.contoso.com on B1
Regional VNet integration is available on B1
exp: Slots and autoscale need Standard or above; managed certificates work on Basic and above; VNet integration is supported on Basic and above.
